quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (year ended March 31, 2026): revenue JPY 1,028,171 million (up 1.4%), operating profit JPY 183,615 million (down 1.1%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 133,498 million (down 2.7%); management states that in its main markets production of IT devices and high-end smartphones exceeded expectations, raising demand for its products, and that nucleic acid contract manufacturing improved as large-disease projects moved from the clinical to the commercial stage; the yen was 1.7% stronger at JPY 150.2 per US dollar, reducing operating profit by JPY 8.1 billion
quarterly_data.figure: revenue JPY 1,028,171 million (+1.4%); operating profit JPY 183,615 million (-1.1%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Industrial Tape segment FY2026 revenue JPY 366,607 million (up 4.2%), operating profit JPY 51,662 million (up 12.6%): demand rose for process materials used in the production of semiconductor memory, ceramic capacitors and the like, and for high-end smartphone assembly materials as more models adopted electric debonding tape for battery fixing; automotive materials revenue fell on lower vehicle production by Japanese automakers in China
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial Tape revenue JPY 366,607 million (+4.2%); operating profit JPY 51,662 million (+12.6%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Optronics segment FY2026 revenue JPY 527,812 million (down 2.6%), operating profit JPY 149,871 million (down 13.4%): information functional materials revenue fell - optical film demand rose on strong high-end laptop and tablet production, but the company continued its strategic withdrawal from optical films for LCD smartphones and cut process protection film prices through material rationalization; circuit materials revenue grew - high-precision board demand rose with expanding high-end smartphone production, and CIS (Circuit Integrated Suspension) stayed robust on demand for high-capacity hard disk drives (HDD) for data centers driven by the spread of generative AI
quarterly_data.figure: Optronics revenue JPY 527,812 million (-2.6%); operating profit JPY 149,871 million (-13.4%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Human Life segment FY2026 revenue JPY 143,702 million (up 8.5%), operating loss JPY 5,041 million (prior year: operating loss JPY 11,718 million): demand rose for nucleic acid contract manufacturing and the nucleic acid materials (NittoPhase) used in it, and production of a large project expected to be commercialized began in the second quarter; membrane revenue fell as demand for polymer separation membranes for industrial uses declined; management expects demand from large projects that moved to the commercial stage to increase and the new NittoPhase plants in Japan and the US, with expanded capacity, to begin full operation; per the R&D section, scale-up technology for nucleic acid process materials was established, full production began at the new plant, and a new processing plant in North America is expected to start operating in the company's fiscal 2026 (the year after fiscal 2025, which ended March 2026)
quarterly_data.figure: Human Life revenue JPY 143,702 million (+8.5%); operating loss JPY 5,041 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 production by segment (at selling prices): Industrial Tape JPY 240,144 million (104.2% of the prior year), Optronics JPY 511,311 million (82.1%), Human Life JPY 137,105 million (110.1%), total JPY 888,564 million (90.9%); the company mainly produces to forecast demand, and build-to-order production is too small a share of sales to report orders

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states the previous medium-term plan 'Nitto for Everyone 2025' met its targets for the year ended March 2026 of operating profit JPY 170 billion and a 17% operating margin (actual JPY 183.6 billion and 17.9%) but missed its 15% ROE target (12.2%); the new medium-term plan 'Nitto RISE 2028' targets operating profit of JPY 220 billion, a 20% operating margin and 14% ROE in the company's fiscal 2028, and operating profit of JPY 240 billion or more, an operating margin of 20% or more and ROE of 15% or more in fiscal 2030 (the company calls the year ended March 2026 fiscal 2025); focus areas are Digital Interface, Green Tech and Human Life, concentrating resources on digital / next-generation telecommunications, semiconductors, environment / renewable energy and life sciences
quarterly_data.figure: fiscal 2028 targets: operating profit JPY 220 billion, operating margin 20%, ROE 14%; fiscal 2030: operating profit JPY 240 billion or more

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management decided a JPY 39 billion investment at the Toyohashi plant, its largest ever, to expand electric debonding tape for battery fixing, whose demand it expects to grow as Europe moves to mandate the right to repair smartphones and other electronics; the new plant is planned to produce electric debonding tape, optically clear adhesive sheets for foldable OLED products and component fixing tape; management also plans to expand sales of process materials for semiconductors and ceramic capacitors in new applications on the spread of generative AI, aiming to raise Industrial Tape's profit margin further

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states that in information functional materials the impact of the semiconductor memory shortage on IT device and smartphone production volumes needs to be watched, while it keeps focusing on high-end products for automotive displays and foldable smartphones

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management expects CIS (Circuit Integrated Suspension) demand to grow as data-center storage demand keeps rising in the HDD market and new technologies such as HAMR (Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording) raise HDD capacity further; for high-precision boards for high-end smartphones it plans new product sales to existing customers for new applications as well as existing ones

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Denko annual securities report: FY2026 (06-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Optronics R&D: the company has productized 'high-precision boards' for smartphones applying its HDD circuit-board technology and is expanding sales and production capacity in printed circuit boards; in fiscal 2025 (the year ended March 2026) it extended the technology to a new application inside smartphones and started mass production; it also deepened work with TruLife Optics (invested in the company's fiscal 2024) on optical components for AR glasses, starting development of low-refractive-index optical materials, and developed PFAS-compliant insulating materials now applied to its own products
